transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-06-10
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Sara Patel (Redwood AE), Miguel Torres (Redwood CSM), Leah Chen (Redwood SE), Mark Johnson (Aurora CTO), Priya Shah (Aurora Head Eng), Elena Ruiz (Aurora Security Lead), Tom Baker (Aurora DevOps)

--- Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect) ---
Sara: quick kickoff, what we want to get done in next 30 days, sandbox, demo, and security questions

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Sara: All right hi everyone thanks for joining, this is Sara from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, with me are Miguel from customer success and Leah our SE; can folks introduce themselves real quick?
[00:12] Mark: Hey all Mark Johnson CTO at Aurora Health, we've got Priya and Elena and Tom on the line.
[00:18] Priya: Hi yes Priya Shah, Head of Engineering.
[00:20] Elena: Elena Ruiz, security.
[00:23] Tom: Tom Baker, DevOps.
[00:25] Sara: Awesome, thanks. The goal for today is to align on objectives for onboarding, success criteria, a rough timeline, and immediate next steps like sandbox access and SSO. If that sounds right we'll move through discovery and then talk tech.
[00:38] Mark: Sounds good. Our primary objective is to replace our existing inference endpoints for clinical summarization and patient routing with something that's predictable cost-wise and low latency. Also we need to meet audit and data residency constraints.
[00:52] Leah: Great. Can you say a bit about current infra? are you hosted on cloud, any VPC constraints, do you need private deployment?
[01:00] Priya: We're on AWS, EKS, and we have a mix of prod and staging clusters. For PII we have stricter controls, we'd prefer private deployment for prod but open to hosted for pilot. We do want SSO and SAML for user access.
[01:12] Tom: Network wise we can do VPC peering, but we'll need IP allowlist details and routes.
[01:17] Elena: From security: SOC2 in scope, need KMS integration for customer-managed keys, audit logs retention and export, and we need to review data retention and deletion policies. Also SOC2 evidence for encryption at rest and transit.
[01:29] Miguel: Totally understood. Our onboarding playbook covers a pilot in a sandbox environment first, then private deployment if you want Dedicated or Private. We'll make sure we capture all the security artifacts.
[01:39] Sara: Quick note on models and latency tradeoffs — Redwood supports hosted API for fast onboarding, Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput, and Private (VPC/on-prem) for strict isolation. For pilot most customers do a hosted sandbox to validate prompts and then move to a Private pilot.
[01:52] Mark: Pricing and cost model — we'll need a sense of token costs and projection. Could you send an estimate for our expected volume?
[02:00] Sara: Yes we'll send a cost projection with estimated tokens per month based on your throughput numbers. Miguel will include the pricing sheet.
[02:06] Priya: For the pilot, what are the integration points? we have a microservice that calls model endpoints, is there a recommended client or SDK?
[02:13] Leah: We provide REST endpoints and SDKs in Python/Node, typical integration is a single API call per request with streaming support. For private deployment you'd also have network routing config and model pinning.
[02:23] Tom: On VPC peering — what's required on our side? any specific subnets or routes?
[02:28] Leah: We'll provide an allowlist of IP ranges for hosted, and for Private we'll work through VPC peering or Transit Gateway. We'll send a network diagram and example Terraform snippets.
[02:39] Elena: KMS — we need customer-managed keys. Is HSM supported?
[02:43] Leah: Yes Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integrations for key wrapping and at-rest encryption. There are a couple of modes, we'll go over them in the SE deep dive. Small note, sometimes docs show K-V cache as K-V cash in exports — sorry for the little typos, but we'll share detailed docs.
[02:58] Mark: Ok good. Timeline-wise we want pilot in the next 3 weeks and prod by end of quarter if all goes well. Is that doable?
[03:06] Miguel: That timeframe is aggressive but doable: week 1 sandbox + prompt tuning, week 2 run benchmarks / latency checks, week 3 private pilot prep and security review. We'll line up resources.
[03:18] Sara: Success criteria — performance (p95 latency below X ms), cost per request below threshold, and passing security checklist. Let's capture exact numbers offline.
[03:26] Priya: For performance, we'll need a small benchmark from Redwood using our prompt set. Can SE run that?
[03:31] Leah: Yes we'll want your sample prompts, expected concurrency and seq lengths. We'll run a benchmark in the sandbox and share the results; note that quantization and batching settings affect throughput and RPS.
[03:43] Tom: About data residency, we process US-only PHI, so we'll need region control. Is Redwood able to pin regions?
[03:50] Leah: Yes hosted regions and Private deployments can be pinned. For Hosted we can pick US regions; for Private you control the infra. We'll document region SLAs.
[03:58] Elena: On audit logs — what format and retention? we need sys logs forwarded to Splunk and also per-token cost reports for finance.
[04:06] Miguel: We provide audit logs via an export, and we can set up a delivery to your S3 or SIEM. Cost breakdown per token and per route is available in Console; we'll share examples.
[04:18] Mark: Ok, security paperwork — do you have an SOC2 cert and a pen test report?
[04:22] Miguel: We're SOC2 compliant, we'll share the attestation and security pack. For pen tests we can share summary/redacted reports and a contact for audit requests.
[04:31] Sara: Next let's align on concrete next steps: we'll need SAML metadata from Aurora, a list of pilot users, network allowlist, and sample prompts. Redwood will provision a sandbox and send the onboarding checklist and security docs.
[04:44] Priya: We'll get SAML and user list by Friday.
[04:46] Tom: I'll pull the network diagram and IP ranges.
[04:48] Elena: I'll share SOC2 scope and audit contact.
[04:51] Leah: I'll follow up to schedule the technical deep dive (VPC, KMS). I'm proposing Tuesday next week but I'll send a Doodle.
[05:00] Miguel: We'll provision a sandbox project and invite the users; you should get invites within 24-48h after we get the user list.
[05:06] Mark: Great. A couple of questions from Priya earlier about migration: How do you handle model versioning and rollout policies?
[05:12] Leah: We support model pinning, rollouts, canary and A/B. You can configure per-route policies and automatic fallback to cheaper model variants. We'll show this in the console demo.
[05:22] Priya: For logging of generated text — can we disable storage or set TTLs?
[05:26] Miguel: Yes you can set retention policies and also opt-out of storing prompts and responses for hosted; Private gives you full control.
[05:33] Sara: Anything else from the Aurora team?
[05:36] Elena: One more: encryption in transit — can you provide certs for mutual TLS for private endpoints?
[05:40] Leah: Mutual TLS is supported for Private deployments, and for hosted we authenticate via API keys + TLS. We'll put details in the SE deep dive.
[05:48] Mark: OK that's helpful. Let's recap action items and deadlines.
[05:53] Sara: Recap: Redwood to send onboarding checklist, pricing, SOC2 attestation; SE to schedule deep dive; CSM to provision sandbox; Aurora to send SAML metadata, user list, network diagram, and security contact. Targets as discussed.
[06:06] Priya: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[06:08] Sara: Thanks all, we'll follow up with notes and links.
[06:12] End of recording.
